title: UFO Researchers Claim They Can Make Mysterious Orbs Appear Just By Thinking About Them
excerpt: golden orb ufo australian outback A group of UFO researchers in Australia says they have discovered a way to make mysterious objects appear in the sky
content:
A group of UFO researchers in Australia says they have discovered a way to make mysterious objects appear in the sky simply by thinking about them.

The Whitehawk Psionics group believes it can communicate with unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) through meditation and mental signals.

NewsNation’s Ross Coulthart recently traveled to Australia to see whether their claims were true. What he found was, to say the least, interesting.

UFO Researchers Claim Mysterious Orbs Respond To Their Thoughts

For a recent episode of Reality Check, Ross Coulthart joined the researchers at Barwon Heads, Victoria, overlooking Bass Strait, where numerous UFO sightings have reportedly occurred.

One member of the group, Steve Carnell, claims he has seen as many as 20 or 30 mysterious glowing orbs over the water in a single night.

“The more the energy of the group lifted, the more orbs that would show up,” Carnell told Ross Coulthart.

The group practices something called CE5, or Close Encounters of the Fifth Kind, where they try to contact UFOs through meditation.

Participants visualize a protective shield and then mentally project a beam of light into space, Whitehawk Psionics leader Troy Gavin explained. They also picture their location from above Earth, hoping whatever is out there will pick up their signal.

Another researcher, Vira Elan, explained how she attempts to communicate with the objects.

“I will normally open myself up or open up that intention and send it out to say, ‘Hi, I’m here,'” said Elan.

Did The UFO Researchers Really Make Something Appear?

During the investigation, Steve Carnell predicted that an object would appear around 7:30 p.m.; indeed, a bright light appeared in the sky about that time. However, the researchers could not tell exactly what it was. Then a second mysterious light was identified as a Cessna airplane.

Parapsychologist Jack Westacott said he felt strange physical sensations during the experiment. “I felt like a high. Felt like drugs,” he said.

The group believes sensations such as tingling and goosebumps may be linked to the UFOs, although Westacott did admit psychological explanations are possible.

“We get that feeling. But when they come really close, that’s when it really gets intense,” he added.

In addition to the orbs the UFO researchers claim to have summoned, Australia has experienced plenty of other strange aerial incidents in recent years.

There was a mysterious burning object that fell from the sky last year, the Australian government’s release of a UFO dossier, and an astrophysicist who suggested an Australian meteor may have been something else entirely. None of these incidents have been confirmed as involving anything extraterrestrial, however.
